newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares post gains at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares post gains at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose at end of weekly trade on Wednesday in dull trade focused mainly on accounts clearing by small traders, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.27 percent to 154.00 points in low 424,595 dinars turnover ($599,710), with activity mostly subdued by the Moslem holy month of Ramadan.

"There was no decline or tangible rise in the market or any bloc sales, with activity mostly focused on end of week speculators settling their exposed accounts," said Nasser al-Amad, head of brokerage firm United Financial Investments.
Small investors usually settle their accounts with brokers at end of weekly trade on Wednesday.

Amad said prices were holding firm despite the poor volume in Ramadan and predicted more brisk activity as company results start to flow after the Eid al-Fitr feast, which celebrates the end of the Moslem fasting month.
Two leading bluechip industrials were the busiest traded stock in a pattern of select activity that continues to buttress the market and prevent price slides.
Bluechip Jordan Cement Factories saw a 0.04 dinar rise to 3.40 dinars in 134,059 dinars worth of trade followed by Arab Potash which rose 0.06 dinars to 5.90 dinars in 38,206 dinars worth of trade.
Vehicle Owners Federation was the top gainer, posting a maximum 5 percent daily rise to 6.30 dinars.

A handful of banks also kept up activity in the banking sector led by Bank of Jordan which posted a 2.58 percent gain to 3.18 dinars. Blue-chip Arab Bank shed 0.250 dinars to 256.25 dinars afer trade worth 25,645 dinars.
Middle East Investment Bank, whose shares are a subject of interest from a French bank, was unchanged at 1.16 dinars.

Jordan Petroleum Refinery rose 0.04 dinars to 9.98 in trade worth 33,938 dinars. The company's stock has risen since Jordan's agreement for supply of cheap Iraqi oil which guarantees it supplies for the rest of the year.
Overall rising shares outnumbered falling shares by 14 to nine, with another 18 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.13 percent to 82.06 points.
